guide.skyblocks.intro:
Shadered+ fills your world with things that move and glow: shader effects, lava lamps, aquariums full of fish, koi ponds, black holes, working solar systems, mirrors that really reflect, portals and whole skies.

Many of them react to music - play a jukebox nearby and watch the dance floors, lasers, visualizers and even the fish move to it.
guide.skyblocks.howto.title: Using this book
guide.skyblocks.howto:
The chapters are down the left, the same groups as the creative tab; a chapter's entries are in the middle, and the one you pick opens on the right: what it does, how to use it and how to make it.

Search the whole guide from the box at the top of the middle column.

Click an item in a recipe to go to its page. Scroll any column with the mouse; Up and Down step through the entries, Left and Right through the chapters, and Prev and Next at the foot of a page turn it.
guide.skyblocks.structure.containment_ch: Put containment frames along all twelve edges of a cube round a singularity, with nothing solid inside. The black hole grows to fill the chamber and it holds far more. The frames then work as the singularity's sides: right-click them, hoppers and pipes on them. Port, display, monitor and redstone frames can take the place of any frame. Shown here at 5x5x5; 7x7x7 and 9x9x9 work too.
guide.skyblocks.structure.containment_ta: Tank frames along the edges of a cube round a whirlpool, glass on all its sides (Tank Glass makes one clear pane, any glass works) and nothing else inside. The whirlpool holds far more and the whole tank fills with its fluids; buckets and pipes work on the frames. Shown here at 5x5x5; 7x7x7 and 9x9x9 work too.

guide.skyblocks.singularity:
A black hole that stores items - lots of them. Build a containment chamber round it to hold far more (see Structures).

Its look can be changed in its screen (the Look button): the black hole, a Dyson sphere (its shell closing panel by panel as it fills), a tesseract (another folded inside for each third) or an item galaxy (spiral arms of little squares in the colours of what it holds).

guide.skyblocks.port_frame: A chamber frame that moves items between the singularity and containers beside it.
guide.skyblocks.display_frame: A chamber frame that shows how much the singularity holds.
guide.skyblocks.monitor_frame: A chamber frame that shows one item and how many of it the singularity holds.
guide.skyblocks.redstone_frame: A chamber frame that gives a redstone signal by how full the singularity is.
guide.skyblocks.whirlpool:
A vortex that stores fluids, each kind swirling down as its own band. Build a containment tank round it to hold far more (see Structures).

Its look can be changed in its screen (the Look button): the whirlpool, a water planet (a band of each fluid, swelling as it fills), bubbles (one or more of each fluid) or a fluid helix (a strand of each fluid, a new helix for every four).

guide.skyblocks.cracked_mirror: A cracked mirror, its reflection broken up by the cracks.
guide.skyblocks.vanity_mirror: A mirror framed with bulbs, like a dressing room's.
guide.skyblocks.infinity_mirror: A tunnel of LED rings going on forever. Side by side on a wall they make one big frame.
guide.skyblocks.infinity_cube: Six half mirrors with LED strips inside: a glowing grid going on forever in every direction. Fill a box with them for one big cube.
guide.skyblocks.portal_mirror: Look through it to see the nearest other portal mirror of the same colour - and walk through to go there.
guide.skyblocks.light_bridge_emitter: Two of these whose light meets make a bridge of solid light you can walk on - up to 64 blocks of it. Put one higher or lower (up to 16 blocks, and nearly as steep as one up for each one along) and the bridge becomes a smooth ramp you walk straight up. Right-click either for its settings: a walkway, a rainbow arch, a moving walkway that carries you along, a wall of light, or a light tunnel that floats you through - and which way it carries, how wide it is (1-3 blocks), its pattern, how bright, glowing rails and its colour.
guide.skyblocks.island_scanner: Scans the area around it into a Sky Island item: a little copy of it, mobs included, to keep and show in paintings, on pedestals or in a weather globe.

guide.skyblocks.oiia_cat:
The spinning cat. Give it redstone to make it spin; 27 of them in a cube make a big one (see Structures).

Feed it a fish (cod or salmon) and it hops off its block: your companion now. It follows you about and does its spin when you pet it (right-click; it also tells you how happy it is). Sneak-right-click to switch between follow, sit and wander: wandering, it keeps to round where you left it (16 blocks) and goes off to its bed, bowl, post, tree, boxes and toys there by itself, even when you're away. Fish heal it; a dye colours its collar, and a name tag gives it a little gold tag.

Give it things to do and it stays happy: a cat bed to nap in, a bowl of fish for when it's hungry, a scratching post, a cat tree to sit on top of, a cardboard box to squeeze into, plushies, a yarn ball, a feather wand, a laser pointer. It naps by anything warm too (a hearth, lava lamps, a magma basin, a lit furnace or campfire, a bed). A happy cat heals by itself, spins for no reason at all, and now and then leaves you a little gift by its bed.

guide.skyblocks.infusion_altar:
Redraw your tools, and paint skies into them. Lay an item on the altar (a sword, a pickaxe, anything from any mod) and right-click it: its texture opens big, like in a paint program.

Next to the tools is the colour you're painting with - click it for a colour picker (any colour at all), or type one (#RRGGBB) - with its shades from dark to light under it, the colours you've used lately, and the colours the item uses. Pick one and draw - recolour pixels, add new ones, rub them out (right mouse) - to make the item look however you like.

On the right are the sky blocks' skies (Shadered's and Shadered+'s): pick one, and the look to see it through (normal, inverted, posterised, blueprint, game boy...), and paint it onto the pixels you want - they become windows into that sky. Under the looks are two sliders. Opacity is how strongly you paint: a sky below 100% lets the item's own pixels show through it, and a colour below 100% mixes with the colour already there. See-through makes the pixels you paint with the colour brush see-through themselves, so you can see through the item (worn armour too) - at 0% opacity it changes only how see-through they are, keeping their colours. Pencil, eraser, bucket fill (shift: that colour everywhere), picker, rectangle and line, brush size, undo and redo. The item turns on the right as it'll look.

Infuse it (an amethyst shard) and the item keeps its new look wherever it is - in your hand, in your inventory, dropped. It changes only how it looks.

guide.skyblocks.moon_jar: Catch the moon. guide.skyblocks.spin_pad: A turntable for OIIA cats - and a generator. The faster it spins, the more Forge Energy it makes (320 FE/t per cat at full speed), passed to anything next to it that takes energy, or kept. Its screen shows how it's going: its speed and turns a minute, the energy it's making and holding. Lay spin pads as a square - 2x2, 3x3 or 4x4 - and they join into a Big Spin Pad: one big plate, its screen taking as many cats as its side cubed (8, 27 or 64), spun together as one big cat, each cat adding 320 FE/t (up to 20,480 FE/t). A tame cat can still hop on a pad by itself, and a cat block set on top still works. A redstone signal stops it. Right-click with a sky block to change the aura's sky.

guide.skyblocks.power_core: Energy storage you can watch fill. Cables and machines put Forge Energy in and take it out (any side, as fast as they like). Alone it holds 1 billion FE; build a core chamber round it (see Structures) and it holds 64 billion, 512 billion or 4 trillion FE, and what it holds grows to fill the chamber. Right-click it for its screen - how much it holds, energy in and out, how long until it's full or empty - and pick its look there: a Pocket Star that swells from a dim ember to a white-hot sun, a Storm that crackles with more and more lightning, a Plasma Globe that sprouts tendrils of light, or an Atom that gains a ring of electrons for every quarter it fills - each lighting the room in its own colour. Energy links (a button on its screen): every block up to 5 away from its chamber that holds energy is listed - set each to Take (the core draws energy from it), Give (the core sends energy to it) or Off; while that page is open they're outlined in the world, green taking, orange giving. A comparator reads how full it is; broken, it keeps its energy.

The core holds far more (64 billion, 512 billion or 4 trillion FE) and what it holds grows to fill the chamber. Its frames work as the core: right-click them, and cables on them put energy in and take it out.

Place it and everything round it - in a circle 4, 8 or 12 blocks wide, from two blocks below it to six above - runs faster: crops and saplings grow (even in the dark - the crystal's light is enough), grass spreads and ice melts sooner (more random ticks), and furnaces, smokers, brewing stands, hoppers and other machines tick again and again. It needs no fuel or energy. Right-click it for its screen: pick the speed (x4, x16, x64 or x256) and the radius, and switch it on or off (also sneak + right-click). While it runs, two rings of runes spin round the crystal, a clock face lights up on the ground, and a dome rises over what it speeds up, its sky racing through day and night - the sun and moon leaving trails, the stars drawing circles - in step with the clock's hands: a day every 2 minutes at x4, every 15 seconds at x256. You can hide the dome from the screen. It doesn't speed up other time crystals, spin pads, power cores or anything that gives energy out (no free energy).

guide.skyblocks.elevator_base: An elevator with a cabin that really rides up and down. Dig or build a shaft 3 blocks by 3, as tall as you like, and put the Elevator Base in the middle of its bottom: floor 1 is on top of it, and its cabin appears there - a floor 3x3 you stand on. On each floor above, cut a 3x3 hole for the shaft and put an Elevator Call Panel beside it (2 to 4 blocks from the shaft's middle), on the floor or on a wall at eye height: that makes it a floor, numbered from the bottom. Right-click a panel to call the cabin. Inside the cabin is a panel of glowing buttons, one for each floor (floor 1 at the bottom left; it's on the side of the shaft with the most wall - or the side you pick on its screen): look at one and click it, and the cabin rides there, carrying everyone in it - you can walk about in it (and jump) as it goes, mobs ride along. The floor it's at is lit, the one it's going to blinks. Right-click the base (or sneak + right-click the cabin or a panel) to pick its look - a Glass capsule with rings of energy up the shaft, a hard-Light platform of glowing hexagons with a trail of light, a soap Bubble pod (the shaft's walls turn to glowing, bubbling water), a Warp cabin (the walls turn to deep space, stars streaking past as you move), a Crystal cabin on a crystal rail, or a Cloud to ride (the walls open onto the sky) - its speed, and the side its buttons and crystal rail are on. Jump on it while it's moving and you ride along too. If something blocks the shaft, it won't go. In its settings, turn on "Redstone at its floor": while the cabin waits at a floor, that floor's call panel gives a redstone signal - a door next to the panel opens as it arrives and shuts as it leaves. It also opens the doors, trapdoors and fence gates right in front of the shaft (one or two blocks out) when the cabin stops at their floor, and shuts them when it leaves - turn it off in its settings. Its size fits the shaft you build over it: the widest clear square (1x1 up to 7x7) all the way up through its floors - so build the hole 2 wide, 4 wide, 5 wide... and its cabin matches. Even sizes sit to whichever side of the base is open. In its settings you can set the size yourself (1x1 to 7x7, or Fit) and the cabin's height (2, 3 or 4 blocks - taller for big mobs).
guide.skyblocks.elevator_panel: Put one beside an elevator's shaft on each floor (see Elevator Base). Right-click: the cabin comes. Choose where to go on the buttons inside the cabin. Sneak + right-click: the elevator's look and speed.
tooltip.skyblocks.hourglass: Right-click: how long, loop, turn it over. Redstone turns it over; run out, it sends a pulse
tooltip.skyblocks.magic_chalk: Draw on the ground; sneak for a rune. Close a ring of chalk round a rune: a magic circle
screen.skyblocks.hourglass.stopped: Stopped - turn it over to start
screen.skyblocks.hourglass.hint: A redstone signal turns it over too
guide.skyblocks.hourglass: A timer you can watch. Right-click it to pick how long its sand runs (1 second to 1 hour), switch looping on or off, and turn it over; a redstone signal turns it over too. The glass spins over in its frame and glowing gold sand pours through the neck, the top sinking into a funnel, a heap growing below. When the sand runs out it gives a short redstone pulse (and chimes) - looping, it turns itself over and runs again, a steady clock. A comparator reads how much sand has fallen.
guide.skyblocks.magic_chalk: Draw magic circles. Right-click the top of a block with the chalk to draw a mark; sneak + right-click to draw a rune (or to turn a mark into one); right-click a rune to change it. Close a ring of chalk round a rune - all around it, 2 blocks away (a 5x5 ring) or 3 (7x7) - and the circle lights up: a glowing circle of runes and a turning star in the rune's colour, light rising off its edge. Inside it (and 3 blocks up) its rune works: Feather - slow falling; Heart - regeneration; Ward - monsters pushed out; Swift - speed; Growth - plants grow, now and then, as with bone meal; Moon - night vision. Break a mark and the circle goes out.
message.skyblocks.spotlight_aiming: Aiming the spotlight: look where it should shine and right-click
tooltip.skyblocks.beam_light: A small white light with a thin beam. Placed, it points the way you're looking. Sneak + right-click: aim it again. Right-click: on / off
guide.skyblocks.beam_light: A small white lamp on a little stand, throwing a thin, bright white beam - on a floor, a ceiling or a wall. It points the way you're looking when you place it: stand behind where it goes, look at what it should light and place it. To point it somewhere else, sneak + right-click it, look where it should shine (it follows your aim) and right-click. Point it at a prism: the crystal splits its white light into rainbows round the room.
tooltip.skyblocks.sonar: Right-click: send a pulse - what it finds lights up through walls. Sneak + right-click: what it finds
guide.skyblocks.sonar: A handheld scanner. Right-click and it sends out a pulse: a glowing ring sweeps out 40 blocks over everything round you, leaving a faint grid of the blocks behind it, and whatever the sonar is set to find lights up as the ring passes it, seen through walls - blocks outlined, mobs glowing - each in its own colour, for a few seconds. Sneak + right-click to choose what it finds: type a block or mob and add it as a block or a mob. A name (minecraft:diamond_ore, zombie), a tag (#c:ores, #minecraft:logs, #minecraft:skeletons) or, for mobs, a kind (monster, creature, water_creature, ambient). Click an entry's colour square to change its colour, x to remove it. (The ring isn't drawn with a shader pack; what it finds still lights up.)
screen.skyblocks.sonar.empty: Type a block or mob first
screen.skyblocks.sonar.no_block: No block or block tag called %s
screen.skyblocks.sonar.no_mob: No mob, mob tag or kind called %s
screen.skyblocks.sonar.nothing: Nothing yet - it won't light anything up
tooltip.skyblocks.echo_field: Whatever moves near it leaves a trail of fading rainbow ghosts. Right-click: how far it reaches
guide.skyblocks.echo_field: Round an echo field, whatever moves - players, mobs, dropped items - leaves a trail of glowing ghosts of itself, red to violet from oldest to newest, each just as it was then, mid-step, fading away: like a long-exposure photo. Right-click it to change how far it reaches: 4, 8 or 12 blocks.
tooltip.skyblocks.phase_block: A wall that burns away with a redstone signal, so you can walk through, and forms again when it stops
guide.skyblocks.phase_block: A wall that opens with redstone. Give it a signal and it goes away so you can walk through; when the signal stops it comes back - and if the signal changes halfway, it turns round from where it is. Phase blocks touching each other are one wall: power any of them and the whole wall opens. Right-click it to choose what the wall looks like - any block (type its name, or use the block in your hand), or its own glowing panel - and how it opens: burning away, in pixels, wiped by a scan line, fading as a hologram, or in a ripple. (It can't be broken while it's open.)
screen.skyblocks.phase.bad: No such block (or one it can't look like)
guide.skyblocks.elevator_sensor: A small sensor for an elevator's landing - on the floor, a wall or the ceiling, within 4 blocks of the shaft and about the floor's height. It gives a redstone signal (to things next to it, and through the block it's on) for that floor. Right-click it to choose when: while the cabin is stopped here, a short pulse as it arrives, a short pulse as it leaves, or while the elevator is moving (for warning lights or a bell).
message.skyblocks.elevator_sensor.here: Floor sensor: while the cabin is here
message.skyblocks.elevator_sensor.arrive: Floor sensor: a pulse when it arrives
message.skyblocks.elevator_sensor.leave: Floor sensor: a pulse when it leaves
message.skyblocks.elevator_sensor.moving: Floor sensor: while the elevator is moving
guide.skyblocks.sky_shapes: Every sky also comes as stairs, slabs, walls, panes, carpets and buttons. Craft them like the stone ones from that sky’s blocks: a pane is a sky block ringed by 8 glass panes, a button a sky block and a stone button.
tooltip.skyblocks.sky_brush.dip: Dip it in a sky: craft it with a sky block
tooltip.skyblocks.sky_brush.use: Hold use and sweep it over blocks to paint their faces
tooltip.skyblocks.sky_brush.wipe: Sneak while brushing to wipe sky paint off
message.skyblocks.sky_brush.dry: The brush is dry: craft it with a sky block to dip it in that sky
guide.skyblocks.sky_brush: Paints a sky onto any block's faces without replacing the block: a starry inlay in a floor, a nebula window in a brick wall. Craft it with a sky block to dip it in that sky, then hold use and sweep it over blocks. Sneak while brushing to wipe paint off; breaking a block takes its paint with it.
screen.skyblocks.studio.name: Name
screen.skyblocks.studio.help: Drag the preview to look around. The layer list is the draw order: lower ones are drawn over higher ones (use the arrows), and the lake mirrors everything above it in the list. Save shares the sky with everyone; Sky blocks swaps your glass for blocks of it (up to 16).
message.skyblocks.studio.glass: Bring glass: each glass block becomes one sky block of this sky
guide.skyblocks.sky_studio: Design your own skies. The server has 8 studio skies: pick one, switch its layers on and off (sky colour, nebula, stars, aurora, sun or moon, shooting stars, horizon grid), set their colours and numbers while the preview changes live, name it and save it for everyone. They are real skies like any other: take sky blocks of one for glass, and its liquid, stairs, slabs, brush paint and creatures all show it.
screen.skyblocks.studio.back: Move back (drawn behind the layer above)
screen.skyblocks.studio.front: Move forward (drawn over the layer below)
tooltip.skyblocks.sky_rift: A crack in the air with a sky behind it. Right-click it with a sky block to choose the sky
tooltip.skyblocks.sky_beacon: Sends a beam of its sky up into the heavens. Right-click it with a sky block to choose the sky
guide.skyblocks.sky_rift:
A jagged crack hanging in the air, always turned to face you, with a sky showing through it as if the world had torn open. Its edges glow and crawl, and little shards drift round it.

Right-click it with any sky block to choose what's behind it (the sky block isn't used up). You can walk through it.
guide.skyblocks.sky_beacon:
A beacon whose beam is made of a sky: a turning column of it rises from the glass case all the way up to the heavens, in a soft glow, and can be seen from far away. Like a beacon's, the beam stops at a solid block.

Right-click it with any sky block to choose its sky (the sky block isn't used up).
tooltip.skyblocks.sky_fountain: Right-click with a sky block to choose its sky; place them side by side for one big fountain
guide.skyblocks.sky_fountain:
A calcite fountain of sky liquid: a two-tiered statue brimming over with sky, a jet of sky leaping from its top and falling in glowing arcs into a pool of sky.

Right-click it with any sky block to choose its sky (the sky block isn't used up). Place them side by side in a rectangle (up to 9 by 9) and they join into one big basin, with one bigger statue in its middle.
guide.skyblocks.water_fountain:
A stone fountain in HD water: a two-tiered statue whose bowl brims over in thin sheets, and a jet leaping from its top and falling in arcs into the pool. The pool ripples, reflects the sky (more the flatter you look), glints in the sun and foams where the water lands, with caustics shimmering under it.

Place fountains side by side in a rectangle (up to 9 by 9) and they join into one big basin, with one bigger statue in its middle.
guide.skyblocks.planet_globe:
A little planet turning on its tilted axis over a copper stand, lit as if by a sun over your shoulder.

Right-click for the next planet: an ocean world (with clouds and city lights on its night side), a gas giant, an ice world, a lava world, a desert world, an alien world, a cratered moon or a toxic world. Sneak and right-click to give it rings or take them away.
guide.skyblocks.aurora_curtain:
A slim rail that an aurora hangs from: folds of light down to the floor (up to 8 blocks), waving slowly, brightest along their lower edge. Curtains side by side hang as one.

Right-click it with a dye for its lower colour; sneak and right-click with a dye for its upper colour.
guide.skyblocks.sky_crystal:
An amethyst shard crafted with a sky block (or a sky liquid bucket): it holds that sky. Use it as an armour trim material at a smithing table - the trim then shows the moving sky itself, on every piece and every pattern.

Craft a sky block (or a sky liquid bucket) with arrows (up to 8 alike), a trident or elytra to give them that sky's glow: arrows and tridents leave a trail of the sky behind them in flight, and elytra behind you as you glide (look back, or switch to third person, to see it).
tooltip.skyblocks.water_fountain: Place fountains side by side (in a rectangle) for one big fountain
tooltip.skyblocks.heat_wand: Right-click a block to make the air over it shimmer with heat (again to stop)
guide.skyblocks.heat_wand:
Heat shimmer makes the air waver over fire, lit campfires, lit furnaces and lava. With the Heat Wand you can give it to any block: right-click the block (again to take it away). Breaking the block takes its shimmer with it.

(Heat shimmer is turned off while a shader pack is in use.)
tooltip.skyblocks.particle_accelerator: In the middle of a flat round ring of accelerator frames (7, 11 or 15 across): give it energy and something to smash - rare things come of the collisions. Right-click it with accelerator frames in your inventory to build the ring (sneak: the smallest)
tooltip.skyblocks.accelerator_frame: A flat round ring of them round a particle accelerator: 7, 11 or 15 across (16, 28 or 40 frames)
tooltip.skyblocks.weather_machine: With weather masts stacked on it: sets the weather (for energy) and catches lightning for energy
tooltip.skyblocks.weather_mast: Stacked on a weather machine: 2 small, 4 medium, 6 large
tooltip.skyblocks.star_forge: In the middle of a cube of forge frames (5 or 7 across): a star you feed fuel - smelts whole stacks, forges alloys, makes energy
tooltip.skyblocks.forge_frame: Along the edges of a 5 or 7 cube round a star forge, its sides open or glass
screen.skyblocks.machine.unformed.accele: Needs a flat round ring of accelerator frames
screen.skyblocks.machine.unformed.weathe: Needs 2 or more weather masts stacked on it
screen.skyblocks.machine.unformed.forge: Needs forge frames along a 5 or 7 cube round it
screen.skyblocks.particle_accelerator.wa: Waiting: give it something to smash
screen.skyblocks.particle_accelerator.no: Needs energy to drive its beams
screen.skyblocks.weather_machine.off: Off: the weather goes its own way
screen.skyblocks.weather_machine.hint: In a storm it draws lightning to its dish
screen.skyblocks.star_forge.idle_smelt: Smelts a whole stack at once
screen.skyblocks.star_forge.hint_forge: Hotter stars forge more (see the guide)
guide.skyblocks.star_forge: A star you feed - the first machine to build. Build forge frames along the twelve edges of a cube round it (5 or 7 across - its sides open or glass, room inside) and a star lights in it when you give it fuel; what you feed it sets its colour. Red: coal, charcoal, coal blocks, dried kelp blocks. Yellow: blaze rods and powder, magma cream, fire charges. Blue: soul sand and soil, ghast tears, echo shards. White: nether stars, end crystals, dragon's breath. The hotter the star, the faster it works and the more energy it gives off - 80, 200, 500 or 1,200 FE/t (more in the 7-wide chamber), given to whatever's beside its frames (a power core, say). Smelting (its screen's button): it smelts a whole stack of anything a furnace can, at once. Forging: alloys - a gold ingot and glowstone dust make Star Gold (yellow star or hotter), an iron ingot and an amethyst shard make Nebula Steel (blue or hotter) - and transmuting: cobblestone to cobbled deepslate, sand to red sand, rotten flesh to leather (2) from red; cobbled deepslate to obsidian (4), quartz to amethyst from yellow; obsidian to crying obsidian, copper to iron (2) from blue; iron to gold (2), coal blocks to a diamond (9) from white. A singularity (or its chamber's frames) beside its frames feeds it what it can work, and takes what it makes. Hoppers and pipes on its frames reach its fuel, its work and what it made. Or power it: with no fuel burning, energy piped into its frames keeps its star lit as the colour picked on its screen (the lightning button) - 200, 500, 1,250 or 3,000 FE/t for red, yellow, blue or white (more in the 7-wide chamber) - working as fuel would, but making no energy. Its alloys build the rest: Star Gold the particle accelerator and the power core, Nebula Steel the weather machine and the singularity's containment frames.
guide.skyblocks.forge_frame: The star forge's frames: along the twelve edges of a 5 or 7 cube round it. Formed, they're its sides - right-click one for its screen, and hoppers, pipes and cables on them reach it.
guide.skyblocks.star_gold_ingot: An alloy from the star forge (gold ingot + glowstone dust, from a yellow star up): for the particle accelerator.
guide.skyblocks.nebula_steel_ingot: An alloy from the star forge (iron ingot + amethyst shard, from a blue star up): for the weather machine.
guide.skyblocks.particle_accelerator: Smashes things for rare loot. Put it in the middle of a flat round ring of accelerator frames - 7, 11 or 15 across (small, medium, large: 16, 28 or 40 frames) - give it energy and an item to smash, and two beams race round the ring opposite ways, faster and faster, drawing more energy the faster they go. At full speed they collide in the middle: the item's gone, and what comes of it lands in its output - redstone, quartz, emeralds and the odd diamond from a small ring; diamonds, echo shards, shulker shells, music discs and netherite scrap from a medium one; netherite, totems, enchanted golden apples, hearts of the sea, even nether stars from a large one (two drops at a time). Run out of energy with the beams going fast and it misfires: a flash, smoke, and the item's lost. Each collision takes about 100k FE (small), 550k (medium) or 2.7M (large). Some things always make the same thing when smashed (many of them made no other way). Any ring: a coal block makes a diamond, leather a saddle, paper a name tag, string 2 cobwebs, dirt 4 grass blocks, gravel 4 flint, a clay ball 2 prismarine shards, a glass bottle 2 bottles o' enchanting. Medium or large: deepslate makes reinforced deepslate, an amethyst block budding amethyst, a golden apple an enchanted golden apple, ancient debris 2 netherite scrap, a nautilus shell a heart of the sea, chorus fruit a shulker shell, a bone block a sniffer egg, sculk an echo shard. Large: prismarine crystals make a trident, an emerald block a totem of undying, a wither skeleton skull a nether star, an eye of ender 4 dragon's breath, a phantom membrane elytra, dragon's breath a dragon egg. To build its ring quickly, right-click it with accelerator frames in your inventory: it builds the biggest ring you have enough frames for (sneak to build the smallest instead; frames already there count).
guide.skyblocks.accelerator_frame: The particle accelerator's ring: a flat circle of them round it (7, 11 or 15 across - 16, 28 or 40 frames), its beams racing round through them.
guide.skyblocks.weather_machine: Sets the weather and catches lightning. Stack weather masts on it (2 or 3 small, 4 or 5 medium, 6 large) and pick Clear, Rain or Storm on its screen: it takes a burst of energy to turn the weather (300k, 500k, 1.2M FE - less the bigger it is), then a trickle to hold it. (The weather's the whole world's, as always in Minecraft.) In a thunderstorm, with open sky over its dish, it draws lightning down to its dish now and then (more often the bigger it is) and catches lightning striking near it - out to 16, 32 or 64 blocks - harmlessly: each strike is 150k, 300k or 600k FE, given to whatever's beside it or its masts (a power core, say), the rest kept to run it.
guide.skyblocks.weather_mast: The weather machine's masts: stacked straight up on it, its dish turning on the top one.
guide.skyblocks.structure.particle_accel: A flat round ring of accelerator frames round the particle accelerator, on its level: 7 across (shown, 16 frames), 11 (28) or 15 (40). Anything can be inside the ring.
guide.skyblocks.structure.weather_machin: Weather masts stacked straight up on the weather machine: 2 or 3 small (shown), 4 or 5 medium, 6 large. Leave open sky over the top one to catch lightning.
guide.skyblocks.structure.star_forge: Forge frames along the twelve edges of a cube round the star forge, its sides open or glass, nothing else inside: 5x5x5 (shown) or 7x7x7.

message.skyblocks.accelerator.blocked: Something's in the ring's way at %s %s %s
jei.skyblocks.forge.smelting_note: Any furnace recipe - a whole stack at once
screen.skyblocks.star_forge.power_tip: With no fuel burning, energy piped into its frames keeps its star lit as a %s star, using %s FE/t (it makes no energy then). Click to change the colour.

screen.skyblocks.power_core.links_help: Blocks up to %s away that hold energy:
tooltip.skyblocks.crafting_frame: A chamber frame: right-click it for the singularity's screen with a crafting grid beside it - take what you need from what it holds, and the grid refills from it as you craft.
guide.skyblocks.crafting_frame: A chamber frame you craft at. Right-click it: the singularity's screen with a crafting grid beside it. Click what it holds to pick it up and lay it in the grid; take what it makes (shift-click: as many as it can) and the grid fills again from what it holds, so you can craft on and on. Clear grid puts it all back; closing the screen does too.
gui.skyblocks.singularity.crafting_hint: Refills from storage as you craft
jei.skyblocks.crafting_frame.needed: Open the singularity from a crafting frame to craft here
jei.skyblocks.crafting_frame.missing: Not in the singularity or your inventory
tooltip.skyblocks.television: Plays YouTube videos and playlists, links to videos, and video files you drag onto its window. Put them together in a wall facing the same way (up to 16 by 12) for one big television
guide.skyblocks.television: A thin flat television. Use it to open its window: paste a YouTube video or playlist link, or a link to a video, and press Play - or drag video files from your computer onto the window (several at once play one after another). Playlists move on by themselves; |< and >| skip back and on, and Repeat starts the list again at its end. Everyone nearby sees and hears the same moment. Build a wall of them facing the same way, up to 16 by 12, and it is one big television. Its sound comes from the screen and fades with distance (the game's Jukebox/Note Blocks volume applies too). Dragged files only play for players who have those files at the same place.
